I checked: L0109 (45.5-49.5), L0114/L0114b (60.5-69), L1504/L1505 (1960.5-1969.5), and the ending plus end cards (2104-2153.5). I also read mix/loudness.json (rides, moments, lineMasking, foley, cue fades), qa/reports/latest.json (17:43Z), the narration/timeline.json word times for every re-taken line, narration/stt.json, voice/voice.json listening and sttHeard, voice/lexicon.json, the script directions for L0114, L0220, L1505 and L1517, the cues.json notes for m01/m19/m21, the m19 spectrogram, and the ch15-s08 and ch15-s09 sheets. summary: Sound clears the bar again, and most round-3 sound items have landed. The first refrain is now clear (L0109 sits about 20 dB over m01), L1517 is unhurried with a real breath, and Amodei is now transcribed literally. The end cards hold a living D at -33 M under the disclosure card and get a celesta on SOURCES. The speech chain is far less pressed: the stem limiter is at 1.05 dB and every line is within 2 dB of the -12 M median. The final 30 s are tight sound-for-picture: stamp, lamp-off, about 2 s of room tone, then the cello walk, the match on 'new' and the flare on 'candles', which the ch15-s09 picture now matches. The master measures -16.0 LUFS, -2.1 dBTP and LRA 5.7, with every cue fade clear of its last strike. The one real regression is L1505. Taking the trim off fixed the shout, but the take decays sharply after 'Nobody', and m19's low floor re-enters on 'told'. 'Nobody told it... to plan' now has the film's thinnest voice margin (8.6 dB, about 4-6 dB broadband on 'to plan'), and it is the only lineLevels failure. L0114's new user wording reads at 221 wpm, which fails QA pacing on the turn into the story. Two of the three STATUS: OPEN stamps are silent. Fix L1505 (a gain envelope or calmer take, plus an m19 re-fit) and slow L0114, and sound moves to about 8.5.

issues.problem: This is an over-correction. With trimDb +0.8, level 'soft' and a -2.1 dB ride computed from the loud 'Nobody' onset, the tail of the take is buried. In narration.wav, 'Nobody' reads -16.5 M, while 'told it' reads -25 to -31 and 'to plan' -24.4 to -26.8, a decay of 8-10 dB within the line. QA lineLevels FAILS (-4.66 dB against the -2 hint), and lineMasking is 8.6 dB, the only line under 10 in the film. In the master, 'to plan' (1967.79-1968.27) reads -20 to -21 M with music around -27 M under it. The line's direction asks for it 'said simply and quietly'. It should be quiet, not masked.
issues.fix: Keep the take's timing (ch15-s03 anchors 'plan' at 13.79). Apply a per-word clip-gain envelope in timeline.mjs: -2 dB on 'Nobody' (1965.84-1966.45) and +4 dB from 'told' to the end of 'plan' (1966.51-1968.27), with 30 ms ramps. Recompute the ride on the enveloped clip, so the loud onset no longer drags the tail down. Alternatively, re-take solo at speed 0.84, spoken 'Nobody told it... to plan.', with stability raised about 0.15 for an even delivery, and keep the take whose 'to plan' is within 4 dB of 'Nobody'. Targets: lineLevels within -2 +/- 1 dB, 'to plan' at -17 M or louder in the master, lineMasking 13 dB or more, and 'Nobody' at -12.5 M or quieter. Re-mix, then confirm the QA lineLevels and lineMasking pass.

issues.problem: The turn into the story, 'Our story starts all the way back in World War Two.' (user wording, 2026-10-13), runs 2.98 s for 11 words, 221 wpm. The direction itself asks for 'the voice's normal pace', and 221 wpm is not this narrator's normal pace.

best_moments: The last 35 seconds: Hinton's quote over the held D, a dry stamp at 2118.25 in clear air, about 2 s of room tone at -57 M, and the lamp click as the room goes black. Then the cello walk under 'Somewhere tonight a lamp is on', the scratch on 'new' and the flare on 'candles', which the picture now matches (unlit match at +21.38, flame standing at +22.79), and celesta M1 in the clear after 'from' into the unresolved Asus4.

The end cards now breathe instead of dying: a ppp A-E + D pad through the Turing card, the lone D held at -32 to -34 M under the disclosure card, one celesta D on SOURCES (-29 M), and a ring-down to the floor exactly at black.

The motto's first statement, 'Put that in the case file.': the music falls to about -35 M under it, the seal's A drops into the breath between 'that' and 'in', and its D closes the drawer after 'file'.

The prologue rewind: the reversed swell is cut dead before 'Our', the 0.8 s pause before 'To a lamp, in Chicago' sits in near silence (-49 M), and about 1.2 s of true silence follows before the title's M1, a scored hush that makes the title land.

Mix hygiene: -16.0 LUFS, -2.1 dBTP, LRA 5.7, a stem limiter at 1.05 dB, every line within 2 dB of the -12 M median, the loudest music moment (the bloom at 2083.5) at -13.8 M in clear air, every cue fade more than 1.6 s past its last strike, and a -58 LUFS room-tone floor.
